communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Dolly Parton
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any main files, see-references, cross-references, and index entries on Anthony Neil Maffatone (born 1943, died Aug. 2, 2000), also known as “Tony Maffatone” and “Little Tony.” Please search all name variants, including “Anthony Nick Maffatone,” “Maffetone,” and the FBI’s own misspellings “Moffatone” and “Muffato.” Search the Central Records System, Sentinel, the Automated Case Support system, the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) indices, and field office indices, including Los Angeles, New York, and Newark.
2. All records in FBI file LA 122A-426, and in any corresponding FBI Headquarters or other field office files, that mention or refer to Anthony Maffatone. This includes the FD-302 of his interview on Nov. 16, 1988, in Los Angeles, which was indexed under “Anthony Neil Moffatone” and transcribed Nov. 29, 1988. It also includes any related FD-302s, 1A envelopes, interview notes, airtels, teletypes, memoranda, and grand jury–related correspondence.
3. All records reflecting communications between the FBI and Anthony Maffatone or his attorney concerning Martin Bacow, Sylvester Stallone, the film productions “Rhinestone,” “Rocky II,” “Cobra,” “Over the Top,” or “Rambo III,” or Maffatone’s stated willingness to testify before a federal grand jury.

Proof of death: Mr. Maffatone died on Aug. 2, 2000, in Suffolk County, New York. Proof of death can be found at the following link: https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/31264411/anthony-maffatone

Because the subject is deceased, his privacy interest is greatly diminished, and Exemptions 6 and 7(C) should not be used to withhold records about him.

For reference, a redacted version of the Nov. 16, 1988, FD-302 was released to me under FOI/PA# 1754808-000. That release withheld 10 pages as “duplicates.” Please process and release those pages in full where they fall within the scope of this request.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: Clearview AI Facial Recognition: SPD Policies, Users, Usage, and Agreements (Savannah PD)

communications.subject: Georgia Open Records Act Request: Clearview AI Facial Recognition: SPD Policies, Users, Usage, and Agreements (Savannah PD)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any policy, general order, standard operating procedure, directive, memo, or training material governing the use of Clearview AI or any other facial recognition tool, including authorized purposes, supervisory approval, case requirements, prohibited uses, retention, auditing, and disclosure to prosecutors or defendants.

2. Documents sufficient to show the number of Clearview AI accounts (seats) the Department has had since March 8, 2024, by unit or role, and the dates each was activated or deactivated. User names may be replaced with rank or unit.

3. Any usage report, administrator dashboard export, or audit log showing the number of Clearview AI searches per month from March 8, 2024, to the date of this request. If the log records a case number, offense type, or stated reason for each search, please include those fields. User names may be replaced with anonymous identifiers that stay consistent across searches.

4. Records sufficient to show any training Department personnel have received on Clearview AI or facial recognition, including dates, who provided it, and the number of attendees.

5. Any agreement, memorandum of understanding, or written arrangement that allows another agency to run searches on the Department's Clearview AI account or share Clearview results with the Department, including SARIC, the GBI, federal agencies, and neighboring agencies.

6. Any accuracy, bias, privacy, or legal-compliance evaluation, vendor demonstration material, or briefing about Clearview AI or facial recognition presented to Department command staff, the City Manager, the Mayor, or City Council.

This request includes records that Clearview AI maintains for the Department, such as its administrator dashboard and usage logs. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a)(2)(B). If any responsive record is withheld in whole or in part, please identify the specific legal authority by Code section, subsection, and paragraph, as § 50-18-71(d) provides, and produce all reasonably segregable portions. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

title: Chatham County Police Department: Vendors Paid, FY2026 and FY2027 to Date (Chatham County Police Department)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A report or export from the County's financial system sufficient to show all vendors paid, or issued a purchase order, on behalf of the Chatham County Police Department for the most recently completed fiscal year (July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026) and for the current fiscal year (beginning July 1, 2026) through the date of this request. Please include the vendor name and, if the system maintains one, the vendor number. If the County's standard vendor or accounts-payable report already includes other fields, such as amounts paid, payment dates, purchase order numbers, or the department or cost center, please leave them in. I am not asking the County to create a new compilation.

This is a request for data fields in the County's financial database. Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(f), please provide it in the format in which it is kept or in a standard export format such as a CSV or Excel file.

If these records are held by the County's Finance or Purchasing Department rather than the Police Department, please forward this request to the appropriate department and let me know where it was sent.

Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1), any labor charge may not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee with the necessary skill and training, and the agency must use the most economical means reasonably calculated to produce the records. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Alabama Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Good day,

I hope this finds you well.

I’m seeking any lists, contracts, MOUs, and data sharing records that outlines which businesses and properties your agency has access. Examples include: Lowes, HOAs, business improvement districts.

I would like to note that the locations of these cameras are made public on OpenStreetMap through DeFlock's mapping work (https://maps.deflock.org/?lat=31.3239&lng=-85.8504&zoom=12.73) This being said, your department personally disclosing their locations can not hurt the system any more than the aforementioned project already has. This negates the idea that department transparency for citizens on this matter is an "operational security threat"

Far more compromising to public safety than a records request, made to peer-review data collected by devices you allow subjecting citizens to, are the well-reported inaccuracies and abuse rates of these devices leading to wrongful detainment, arrest, officer misuse and credential breaches. 

Logins to Flock systems are available for purchase on the 'darknet'. Also, the cameras have been shown, contrary to Flock Safety statements, to store image captures and authorization keys on each device- even someone with a hacksaw could use the data for their own purposes, not just the blatantly corrupt federal agencies ALPR systems share data with.

Furthermore, with the Supreme Court ruling in Chatrie v United States (2026), these devices are unconstitutional. The federal government, superseding state legislation, ruled an expectation of privacy in location data which reveals your movements in the physical world, and even short-term surveillance of these movements is a search subject to the Fourth Amendment. 

Hiring a third-party should not allow courting Constitutional violations.

This information may also be found in Flock Safety or other ALPR company emails that alert the department that a business or private entity is sharing their cameras with you; no new records creation will be necessary- only use of existing records- though creation would be a valuable use of taxpayer money, given the mounting public interest in surveillance technology.

Please search 2023 to today’s date.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

André Natta, a citizen of Alabama, in coordination with Jonathan Harris.

title: Dayton Open Records Request- Eviction Data

communications.subject: Ohio Open Records Law Request: Dayton Open Records Request- Eviction Data
communications.communication:
Dear Open Records Coordinator,

I am writing on behalf of the Data Acquisition Lab to formally request access to public records under the Ohio Open Records Law, §149.43 et seq. We are requesting local eviction information for data visualization and analysis, which will enable a more meaningful understanding of community-level housing and displacement trends. We plan to request this information on a quarterly basis going forward.

I am specifically requesting the following information related to eviction filings in the City of Dayton, spanning from January 1st, 2026 to present:
• Case Number
• Case Type
• Court Date
• Filed Date
• Reason for Eviction Filing (i.e., nonpayment of rent, lease violations, etc.)
• Hearing Date
• Hearing Time
• Case Disposition (if applicable)
• Plaintiff Name
• Plaintiff Address
• Plaintiff City
• Plaintiff Zip
• Plaintiff Phone Number
• Defendant Name
• Defendant Address
• Defendant Address Unit
• Defendant City
• Defendant Zip
• Defendant Phone Number
• Monthly Rent (monthly contracted rent amount)
• Amount Owed by the Defendant (if applicable)
• Subsidy Amount Received, if Available (i.e., government subsidy for rent -- like from a voucher)

If possible, please provide the dataset as a .CSV file, with one row per case, including the above fields, and notify me in advance of any necessary clarification or related costs exceeding $100.

If certain records or portions of records are exempt from disclosure, please provide a written explanation of the specific exemption(s) and release any non-exempt portions of the requested records.

Thank you for your attention to this request. If you have any questions or require further information, please feel free to contact me.
